chunks.text: It's Wednesday, April 29th. Here's what actually moved in AI in the last 24 hours.
Okay Jordan, lead story — Anthropic shipped something called "Claude for Creative Work." What is it?

It's a coordinated MCP connector rollout, and the partner list is the interesting part. Adobe across 50-plus Creative Cloud apps, Blender, Autodesk Fusion, Ableton, Splice, Canva's Affinity, Resolume, and SketchUp. All landed yesterday, April 28th, per Anthropic's own announcement.
So Claude can now drive Photoshop and Blender directly?

Through their APIs, yes — but the part I care about is that these are MCP connectors. Any MCP-aware client can use them. It's not a Claude lock-in play. Anthropic also joined the Blender Development Fund as a patron and seeded RISD, Ringling, and Goldsmiths with access.
Why does that matter beyond "cool, AI in Photoshop"?

Because it's the first time a frontier lab has coordinated a multi-vendor push into pro creative tooling. It's a real stress test of whether MCP becomes the de facto agent integration layer or stays a dev-tools protocol. That's the actual signal.
Speaking of MCP — wasn't there an OX Security disclosure still hanging over it?

Yeah, The Hacker News reported the design-vulnerability ripple is ongoing — STDIO command execution across roughly 200,000 instances, CVE-2026-30623 filed against the MCP SDK, and Anthropic is publicly calling it "expected behavior." So this big creative push is happening while the protocol's security model is contested. Worth flagging.
Noted. Story two — NVIDIA dropped an open model?

Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, also April 28th. Open weights, open datasets, open training recipes. It's a 30 billion parameter hybrid MoE with 3 billion active, 256K context, and it ingests text, image, audio, video, documents, charts, and UI screenshots.
Three billion active parameters — that's deployable territory.

That's the thread. NVIDIA is positioning this squarely at the agent perception layer — computer use, document parsing, video reasoning. They claim it tops six leaderboards in document intelligence and audio-video understanding, and roughly 9x throughput versus other open omni models at comparable latency.
What's actually new there?
The 9x number, if it holds. But it's a vendor self-report on release day. Independent benchmarks haven't landed yet, so I'd hold the applause until someone outside NVIDIA confirms it.
Anything else on the open-model front?

Quick mention — DeepSeek V4-Pro from last week, 1.6 trillion total, 49 billion active, MIT-licensed, 1 million context. Per DeepSeek's API docs they're claiming Codeforces 3,206 and 80.6 percent on SWE-bench Verified, putting it 0.2 points behind Claude Opus 4.6. Geeky Gadgets is already reporting independent reviews are mixed on whether it actually closes the gap outside the published benchmarks.
And one for the SDK watchers?

The Claude Agent SDK shipped four minor versions in 13 days on npm — v0.25 through v0.29.2. Notable change: the explicit "opus" model string is now aliased to "default," and there's a dynamic-models payload. If you're embedding it, go read the changelog before you upgrade.
Punchy day. Connectors, an open omni model, and an SDK that won't sit still.
That's the read.
